## 1. Introduction and agreement

### 1.1 What these terms are
These Terms of Service ("Terms") are a legal agreement between you and the
individual who publishes the NexLink Products ("the Operator", "we", "us").

**One agreement covers every NexLink Product.** Appendix A lists them. You accept
these Terms once, and they apply to each Product you use. Where a clause applies
to only one Product it says so.

### 1.2 Acceptance
By creating an account, or by using a NexLink Product that does not require an
account, you confirm that you have read these Terms, the Privacy Policy and the
Content Policy, and that you accept them. If you do not accept them, do not use
the Products.

Acceptance is recorded against the version number of each document. A material
change requires you to accept again before continuing.

### 1.3 Documents forming this agreement
- These Terms of Service
- The Privacy Policy
- The Content Policy
- The Data Retention Schedule
- **Appendix A — Definitions**, at the end of this and every other document

The Transparency Note, the Law Enforcement Guidelines and the Security
Disclosure Policy are explanatory and do not form part of the agreement, but
they are accurate and you may rely on them as descriptions of how the Products
behave.

### 1.4 Definitions
Defined terms are set out in **Appendix A** at the end of this document. Appendix
A is identical in every NexLink legal document.

## 2. The Products

### 2.1 NexLink
An SMS, dialler and unified-inbox application for Android. It works on your
device and with your mobile carrier. It requires no account with the Operator
and, used alone, sends nothing to the Operator's servers.

### 2.2 NexLink Social
A private, invite-only messaging and calling service using the Matrix protocol
with end-to-end encryption. It requires an Account and an Invite.

### 2.3 NexLink for Wear OS
A companion to NexLink for smartwatches. It holds no account of its own.

### 2.4 NexLink Bridge
The Computer Bridge built into NexLink, together with its browser client. It
sends your messages to **a server you host yourself**, at an address you enter.
There is no default server and no server of the Operator's involved — see
Privacy Policy §3.0.

### 2.5 The Products are independent
Installing or using one Product does not require another, and deleting one does
not affect another. They share a developer and a signing key; they do not share
your data except where a Product explicitly offers that and you enable it.

### 2.6 What the Products are not
- **Not** a business, a company, or a commercial product.
- **Not** operated by a team, and with no support department.
- **Not** a telecommunications carrier. **You cannot call emergency services
  through NexLink Social.** NexLink's dialler places calls through your own
  carrier, and emergency calling is your carrier's function, not ours.
- **Not** a records-retention or archiving system.

### 2.7 No charge, and voluntary donations
The Products are provided **free of charge**. There are no fees, no
subscriptions, no in-app purchases, and no advertising. Nothing about you is
sold.

**A donation page exists.** The Operator links to a third-party donation page
(Buy Me a Coffee) from within the Products. If you choose to use it:

- Donations are **entirely voluntary** and are a gift to the Operator, not
  payment for the Service.
- Donating **confers no benefit whatsoever** — no additional features, no
  priority support, no increased capacity, no different treatment under the
  Content Policy, and no service level commitment. The Service you receive is
  identical whether you donate or not.
- Donations are **not refundable**, because nothing was purchased.
- The donation is a transaction between you and the third-party provider. **The
  Operator never receives or stores your card or bank details.** What the
  Operator receives is described in the Privacy Policy.
- Choosing not to donate has no consequence of any kind.

### 2.8 Future charges
We may introduce charges for a future Product or feature. If we do, you will be
told in advance, no existing free function will become paid without notice, and
you may delete your Account rather than accept them.

## 3. Eligibility and registration

### 3.1 Minimum age
**You must be at least 16 years old** to use any NexLink Product.

You must confirm this when you create an Account. We do not collect your date of
birth; only the confirmation is recorded. If we become aware that an Account
belongs to someone below the minimum age, it will be removed.

This single age applies in both Permitted Territories. It is set at 16 because
that is the higher of the two thresholds the Operator could reasonably be held
to, and applying one number everywhere is clearer than applying two.

### 3.2 Invitation required
Accounts on NexLink Social can only be created with a valid, unspent Invite.
There is no open registration.

### 3.3 Accuracy
You must not impersonate another person or create an Account using a name
intended to deceive.

### 3.4 One person per Account
An Account is personal to you. You may use it on as many of your own Devices as
you wish, but you must not share it with another person.

### 3.5 Username permanence
Your username is permanent. It cannot be changed, and after deletion it is never
reissued to anyone else — including you.

### 3.6 Capacity
You confirm that you have the legal capacity to enter into this agreement. If
you are between 16 and the age of majority in your jurisdiction, you confirm
that you have the capacity of judgement required by the law of your Permitted
Territory to do so.

### 3.7 Permitted Territories — where the Service is offered
**The Service is offered only to Users resident in Switzerland or Australia.**

These are the two jurisdictions whose law the Operator has written these
documents to comply with, and whose authorities the Operator can answer to. The
Operator does not offer the Service in, and does not direct it at, any other
country.

By using the Service you confirm that you are resident in one of them. If you
move outside both, you should stop using the Service and may delete your
Account.

**You must comply with the law of your own Permitted Territory as well as with
these Terms.** These Terms are not a substitute for that law and do not permit
anything it forbids. Where the two differ, the law governs and these Terms apply
only to the extent they are consistent with it.

**Honest limits of this clause:**
- The Operator does **not** verify your location, does not collect location
  data, and does not geo-block. This clause states where the Service is offered;
  it is not a technical control.
- Travelling temporarily outside a Permitted Territory does not breach these
  Terms.
- If you use the Service from a third country, you do so on your own initiative
  and you are responsible for whether that is lawful where you are. The Operator
  makes no representation that the Service is lawful outside the Permitted
  Territories, and encryption is restricted or prohibited in some countries.

## 4. Your account and its security

### 4.1 Your responsibilities
You are responsible for:
- Keeping your password secret.
- Keeping your Recovery Key safe.
- Securing the Devices you sign in on, including setting a screen lock.
- All activity that occurs under your Account.

### 4.2 The recovery warning — read this
**If you lose both your password and your Recovery Key, your message history
cannot be recovered by anyone, including the Operator.**

This is not a limitation we could remove with more effort. It is a direct
consequence of end-to-end encryption: we do not hold the keys, so there is
nothing for us to restore. No support request can change this.

### 4.3 Device verification
You are responsible for verifying your own Devices. A Device you have not
verified may be unable to read your message history, and an unexpected Device
appearing on your Account is a signal you should investigate rather than ignore.

### 4.4 Compromise
If you believe your Account has been compromised, change your password
immediately and remove unrecognised Devices from the Devices screen. Removing a
Device stops future access. **It does not remove messages already on that
Device.**

## 5. Acceptable use

### 5.1 The Content Policy
The Content Policy forms part of these Terms and describes prohibited content
and conduct in detail. You must comply with it.

### 5.2 Summary of prohibited conduct
You must not use the Service to:
- Do anything **Unlawful** as defined in Appendix A — that is, unlawful under
  the law of your own Permitted Territory.
- Harass, threaten, stalk or intimidate any person.
- Share child sexual abuse material. This results in immediate removal and
  reporting to the relevant authority.
- Share intimate images of a person without their consent.
- Promote, incite, instruct in or solicit participation in **Terrorism** or
  **Violent Extremism**, each as defined in Appendix A.
- Distribute malware, or attempt fraud or phishing.
- Attempt to breach the security of the Service, guess Invite codes, or
  interfere with its operation.
- Evade a block, suspension or removal, including by creating a new Account.
- Use automated means to create Accounts or send messages at scale.
- Resell or commercially exploit access to the Service.

### 5.3 What these prohibitions do not cover
The definitions in Appendix A are deliberately narrow and each carries an express
exclusion. **Advocacy, protest, dissent, satire, journalism, research, historical
documentation and artistic depiction are not prohibited**, and the Operator will
not treat them as prohibited, even where the subject matter is disturbing or the
opinion expressed is unpopular.

A prohibition a user cannot predict is not a fair prohibition. If you cannot
tell from Appendix A whether something is permitted, ask before assuming it is
not.

### 5.4 Encryption is not a defence
That the Operator cannot read your messages does not make prohibited conduct
acceptable. Reports from the people you communicate with are actionable without
the Operator reading anything.

### 5.5 Reporting and blocking
You may block any user immediately, without involving the Operator. You may also
report a user; reports may include message content **only if you explicitly
agree** at the time.

## 6. Your content

### 6.1 You own it
You retain all rights in the Content you create. These Terms do not transfer
ownership of anything to the Operator.

### 6.2 The limited licence you grant
You grant the Operator only the licence technically necessary to operate the
Service: to store, transmit and deliver your Content to the recipients you
choose.

Because your Content is end-to-end encrypted, in practice this is a licence to
store and forward data we cannot read. It does not permit us to use, analyse,
publish or disclose your Content, and we could not do so if we wished to.

### 6.3 What others can do with what you send
**Anyone you send a message to can save, screenshot, copy or forward it.**
Encryption protects your message in transit and at rest on our servers. It
cannot control what a recipient does after they receive it. Do not send anything
you would not want kept.

### 6.4 Backups of your own content
Your message history lives on your Devices. Exporting it is your responsibility
and the Service provides a tool for it. The Operator cannot export it for you,
because the Operator cannot read it.

## 7. Availability, changes and discontinuation

### 7.1 No service level agreement
**There is no uptime guarantee, no service level agreement, and no support
commitment.**

The Service runs on hardware in a private residence, on a domestic internet
connection, administered by one person who has other commitments. It may be
unavailable at any time, without notice, and for as long as it takes that person
to notice and fix it.

### 7.2 Do not rely on it
**Do not use this Service for any purpose where unavailability, delay or data
loss would cause you serious harm**, including medical, financial, legal or
safety-critical communication. Use a service with a support contract for those.

### 7.3 Emergency services
**NexLink Social cannot be used to contact emergency services.** Calls made
through it are internet calls between accounts and do not reach 000, 112, 117,
144 or any other emergency number.

### 7.4 Maintenance and changes
We may change, suspend or remove features at any time. Where a change removes
something you depend on, we will give what notice is practical.

### 7.5 Where the servers are
The Service's servers are currently in Australia. **The Operator may move them
to Switzerland or operate in both countries.** If the location of your Personal
Data changes, the Privacy Policy will be updated and you will be told before the
move, because it changes which authority supervises your data and which country's
law applies to it in transit.

### 7.6 Discontinuation
The Operator may discontinue any Product or the whole Service. If that happens:
- You will be given as much notice as is practical, and not less than 30 days
  where the decision is within the Operator's control.
- Your Content remains exportable throughout the notice period.
- After shutdown, data is deleted. There is no archive.

Where the Service ends because of circumstances outside the Operator's control —
hardware failure, loss of the residence, illness — notice may not be possible.
This is a real risk of a solo-operated service and you should keep your own
exports accordingly.

## 8. Suspension and termination

### 8.1 By you
You may delete your Account at any time:
- In the app, under Settings; or
- At `https://nexlink.thvjq.com.au/delete/`, which works without the app
  installed.

No reason is required and no approval is needed.

### 8.2 By the Operator — for cause
Your Account may be suspended or removed if:
- You breach these Terms or the Content Policy.
- You use the Service unlawfully.
- Continuing to provide the Service to you would put other users at risk.
- You are the subject of multiple credible reports.

### 8.2a By the Operator — at discretion, without cause

**The Operator may suspend or remove your Account, or withdraw your access to
any NexLink Product, at any time, for any reason or for no reason, with or
without notice, and without being required to give a reason.** This right
belongs to the Operator, to anyone acting on the Operator's behalf, and to
anyone to whom the Service is transferred under clause 10.2.

It is not limited to the grounds in clause 8.2, and the Operator does not have
to show that any of them applies.

**Why the Operator has this right, and why it is fair that they do:**

- **You have exactly the same right.** Clause 8.1 lets you delete your Account
  at any time, for any reason or none, with no notice, no explanation and no
  approval. Neither party is tied to the other, and neither has to justify
  leaving.
- **Nothing has been paid.** The Service is free (clause 2.7). No fee, no
  subscription and no purchase is lost, and a donation buys nothing and
  therefore loses nothing.
- **Your content stays yours.** Your message history lives on your Devices, not
  on the Operator's server in readable form, and the export tool is yours to use
  (clause 6.4). Removal ends your access to the Service; it does not take your
  messages from you.
- **This is one person running a service from home.** The alternative to a
  discretion like this is an obligation to keep serving someone the Operator has
  a reason — possibly a reason they cannot safely explain — not to serve.

**What this right does not do:**

- It does **not** override clause 9.1. Any guarantee, right or remedy that the
  law does not permit to be excluded is unaffected, including the Consumer
  Guarantees for a user in Australia and the mandatory provisions of Swiss law
  for a consumer in Switzerland.
- It does **not** permit the Operator to act unlawfully. It is not a right to
  remove you on a ground that the law of your Permitted Territory prohibits,
  including a ground of discrimination.
- It does **not** affect the data you are entitled to. Deletion follows clause
  8.5 and the Privacy Policy either way, and your rights of access and
  portability survive removal.

### 8.3 Process, and what is practice rather than entitlement
**Where the Operator acts under clause 8.2, you will where practical be told
what happened and why, and may appeal** by contacting the Operator through the
Contact Page. Where the breach involves illegal material or an immediate risk to
another person, removal may be immediate and without notice.

**Where the Operator acts under clause 8.2a, no reason is owed to you.** The
Operator's usual practice is still to explain and to accept an appeal, because a
service that removes people silently is one nobody should trust — but that is a
practice the Operator follows, not a right you hold, and clause 8.2a is not
conditional on it.

This distinction is drawn openly instead of leaving two clauses to contradict
each other. A document that promises an explanation in one place and reserves an
unexplained discretion in another has told you nothing about which you will get.

### 8.4 Invite accountability
Invites form a tree that records who invited whom. An Account that repeatedly
invites users who are removed for abuse may itself be actioned. This is
disclosed here so that inviting someone is understood as carrying some
responsibility.

### 8.5 Effect of termination
On deletion, your Account, profile, uploaded files, encrypted backup, email
address and connection records are removed. Three things are kept, with reasons
given in the Privacy Policy: your tombstoned username, the record that you
accepted these Terms and confirmed your age, and the Invite record.

Deleted data persists in encrypted database backups for up to 14 days before
those backups expire.

Nothing in section 9 is intended to operate as such a term. If a clause would

Subject to clauses 9.1 to 9.3, the Service is provided "as is" and "as

**This limitation does not apply to loss caused by the Operator's unlawful

### 9.6 Your indemnity
You agree to indemnify the Operator against claims, losses and costs arising
from your breach of these Terms, your unlawful use of the Service, or your

This indemnity does not apply to the extent the claim arises from the Operator's

### 9.7 Third-party services
The Service depends on third parties, listed in the Privacy Policy. The Operator
is not responsible for their acts or omissions, and their outage is an outage of

## 10. General

### 10.1 Notices
Notices to you may be given in the app, by email if you provided one, or by a

**Notices to the Operator go to the address published on the Contact Page** —

### 10.2 Assignment
You may not assign these Terms. The Operator may assign them on transfer of the

### 10.3 Severability
If any provision is unenforceable, it is severed and the remainder continues.

### 10.4 Waiver
A failure to enforce a provision is not a waiver of it.

### 10.5 Entire agreement
These Terms and the documents in clause 1.3 are the entire agreement between you
and the Operator about the Service.

### 10.6 Force majeure
The Operator is not liable for failure to perform caused by events beyond
reasonable control, including hardware failure, power or internet outage, or the

### 10.7 Dispute resolution
If you have a complaint, contact the Operator first through the Contact Page.
Most problems are misunderstandings and are resolved that way. If a dispute is
not resolved within 30 days, either party may pursue it in the courts identified
in clause 10.9.

### 10.8 Governing law
- **If you are resident in Australia**, these Terms are governed by the laws of
  New South Wales, Australia.
- **If you are resident in Switzerland**, these Terms are governed by Swiss law.

Where you are a consumer, this clause does not deprive you of the protection of
the mandatory rules of the law of your own country of habitual residence. For a
consumer resident in Switzerland, Article 120 of the Federal Act on Private
International Law applies the law of Switzerland to contracts for services of
ordinary consumption intended for personal use, and a choice of a different law
is not effective against you.

### 10.9 Jurisdiction
- **Users resident in Australia** submit to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of
  the courts of New South Wales.
- **Users resident in Switzerland** may bring proceedings at the court of their
  own domicile, and nothing in these Terms requires a Swiss consumer to litigate

### 10.10 Changes to these Terms
These Terms are versioned. A material change requires re-acceptance in the app.
Minor corrections may be made without re-acceptance, and the version history is
available on request.

### 10.11 Language
These Terms are published in English and German. Where the two differ, the
English version prevails, except where clause A.5 of Appendix A provides
otherwise for a Swiss consumer.

### 10.12 Contact
The Operator, at the address published on the **Contact Page**:
`https://thvjq.com.au/nexlink/contact`

## Appendix A — Definitions

This appendix is identical in every NexLink legal document. It is maintained as a
single source and appended mechanically, so a term cannot come to mean one thing
in the Terms of Service and another in the Content Policy.

Where a term is defined by reference to a statute, the statutory definition
governs and this text is a plain-language summary of it. Where the statute and
this summary differ, **the statute prevails**.

### A.1 The service and the parties

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **NexLink Products** | All software published by the Operator under the NexLink name. At the date of this version: **NexLink** (SMS, dialler and unified inbox for Android), **NexLink Social** (encrypted messenger for Android), **NexLink for Wear OS**, and **NexLink Bridge** (the Computer Bridge in NexLink together with its web client). A product added later is covered from the date it is published. |
| **Service** | Whichever NexLink Products you use, and the server infrastructure that supports them. |
| **Operator** | The individual who publishes the NexLink Products and runs the Service. Contact details are published at the Contact Page. |
| **Contact Page** | `https://thvjq.com.au/nexlink/contact` — the single published source for the Operator's contact details, kept current so that a notice address embedded in an installed application can never go stale. It publishes an email address; a postal address is supplied on request and to any authority or party entitled to it. |
| **You**, **User** | The natural person who has accepted these documents and uses the Service. |
| **Account** | Your identity on a NexLink Product that requires registration. |
| **Device** | A phone, tablet, watch or computer signed in to your Account or running a NexLink Product. |

### A.2 Data and content

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Content** | Anything you send, receive, upload, store or transmit using the Service. |
| **Metadata** | Information generated by your use that is not Content — who communicated with whom and when, message sizes, IP addresses, device identifiers. The Privacy Policy states exactly which items exist. |
| **End-to-end encryption** | Encryption in which only the participating Devices hold the decryption keys, and the Operator does not. |
| **Personal Data** | Has the meaning given by Article 5(a) of the Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection (FADP) for Users in Switzerland, and the meaning given to "personal information" by section 6 of the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) for Users in Australia. Both mean, in substance: any information relating to an identified or identifiable person. |
| **Recovery Key** | The code that restores access to your encrypted message history. The Operator does not hold a copy and cannot reissue it. |
| **Invite** | A single-use code required to create an Account on an invite-only NexLink Product. |

### A.3 Prohibited-conduct terms

These four definitions exist because a prohibition a user cannot predict is not
a fair prohibition, and because enforcement against vaguely defined conduct is
both unjust and legally fragile. Each is drawn from statute and each carries an
express exclusion.

#### **Terrorism** / **Terrorist Act**

For a User in **Australia**, as defined by section 100.1 of the *Criminal Code Act 1995* (Cth): an action or threat of action that

1. causes death, serious physical harm, serious damage to property, endangers life, creates a serious risk to public health or safety, or seriously interferes with essential electronic systems; **and**
2. is done with the intention of advancing a political, religious or ideological cause; **and**
3. is done with the intention of coercing or influencing by intimidation a government, or intimidating the public or a section of the public.

For a User in **Switzerland**, as understood by Articles 260ter and 260quinquies of the Swiss Criminal Code (StGB/CP) and the *Federal Act on Police Measures to Combat Terrorism*: participation in, support of, or financing of an organisation that pursues its aims through crimes of violence, or the commission of such crimes to intimidate a population or coerce a state or international organisation.

> **Express exclusion.** Advocacy, protest, dissent, satire, journalism, academic
> research, historical documentation, artistic depiction and industrial action
> are **not** terrorism, and are not prohibited by any NexLink document, unless
> the conduct itself satisfies every limb of the definition above. All three
> limbs of the Australian definition must be met; any one alone is not enough.
> This exclusion mirrors section 100.1(3) of the Criminal Code and is stated
> here so that no reader has to find it.

#### **Violent Extremism**

Neither Australian nor Swiss law supplies a single statutory definition, so the
Operator adopts a deliberately narrow one and states it rather than leaving it
to be inferred:

Content or conduct that **intentionally promotes, incites, instructs in, or
solicits participation in unlawful violence against a person or group** by
reason of their race, religion, nationality, ethnicity, sex, gender identity,
sexual orientation, disability, or political opinion.

> **Express exclusion.** Reporting on, condemning, analysing, satirising,
> educating about, or counter-speaking against violent extremism is **not**
> violent extremism. Describing an event is not promoting it. Holding or
> expressing an unpopular, offensive or radical political or religious opinion
> is **not** violent extremism and is not prohibited; the prohibition attaches
> to the incitement of unlawful violence, and to nothing else.
>
> The Operator will not treat a User as engaged in violent extremism on the
> basis of their political or religious beliefs, their nationality, or their
> association with others, in the absence of the intentional incitement
> described above.

#### **Proscribed Organisation**

An organisation listed as a terrorist organisation under Division 102 of the
*Criminal Code Act 1995* (Cth), or subject to prohibition or sanction under the
Swiss *Embargo Act* or Federal Council ordinance. The Operator applies the list
of the jurisdiction in which the User is located, and does not maintain a list
of its own.

#### **Unlawful**

Contrary to the law of Switzerland or of the Commonwealth of Australia and the
Australian State or Territory in which the User is located. Where conduct is
lawful in the User's own jurisdiction it is not "unlawful" under these documents
merely because it is unlawful elsewhere.

### A.4 Legal and jurisdictional terms

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Permitted Territories** | Switzerland and Australia. The Service is offered only to Users resident in these two countries — see Terms of Service §3.7. |
| **FADP** | The Swiss *Federal Act on Data Protection* of 25 September 2020, in force 1 September 2023, together with the Data Protection Ordinance (DPO). |
| **FDPIC** | The Swiss *Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner* (EDÖB/PFPDT), the supervisory authority for Users in Switzerland. |
| **Privacy Act** | The *Privacy Act 1988* (Cth) and the Australian Privacy Principles made under it. |
| **OAIC** | The *Office of the Australian Information Commissioner*, the supervisory authority for Users in Australia. |
| **ACL** | The *Australian Consumer Law*, Schedule 2 to the *Competition and Consumer Act 2010* (Cth). |
| **Consumer Guarantees** | The guarantees given by the ACL that cannot be excluded, restricted or modified by agreement. |

### A.5 Reading these documents

- **"Including"** means "including without limitation".
- **"Writing"** includes electronic messages sent to the address on the Contact Page.
- Headings are for navigation and do not affect interpretation.
- A reference to a statute is a reference to it as amended, and to any statute that replaces it.
- Where the English and German versions of a document differ, **the English version prevails**, except where the User is a consumer resident in Switzerland and Swiss law requires otherwise.
